answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because bridge only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, pearl is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any relic approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
